data.credibility: Management frequently guides long-term goals but displays mixed follow-through in the short term, occasionally dropping or omitting updates on specific capex and revenue projections while maintaining others.

lines.line: Working capital cycle target of 50 to 55 days was actually reported at 11 days.
Export contribution target of greater than 10% by FY2030 remains on track.
FMEG EBITDA margin target of 8% to 10% by FY2030 achieved 10.1%.
EHV plant commissioning by the end of next calendar year was marked delayed.
Project Spring annual capex guidance of 12 billion to 16 billion rupees was dropped.
BharatNet orders expected to generate 4.5 billion rupees over 3 years remains on track.
BharatNet project O&M expected to generate 3.5 billion rupees over 10 years was dropped.
Dividend payout ratio target of 30% by financial year 2030 was dropped.
Planned capex program of 60 billion to 80 billion rupees over 5 years was dropped.
Wires and Cables margin guidance of 11% to 13% achieved 14.1% so far.
FMEG business growth expectation of 1.5x to 2x industry growth remains on track.
EPC sustainable operating margins in high single digits achieved 14.1% so far.

bull: Revenue compounded 26.9% and net profit 25.0% annually over five years, supported by a TTM revenue of 34,609 cr.
The company is almost debt-free with a low debt-to-equity ratio of 0.02, backed by borrowings of 272 cr against net worth of 13,094 cr.
Operating cash flow reached 101% of reported profit over five years, and working-capital days tightened from 67 to 30.
bear: Management has dropped or omitted several major targets, including Project Spring capex guidance and the 5-year capex program of 60 to 80 billion rupees.
The valuation is elevated with a P/E ratio of 37.7, despite strong historical growth numbers.
Segment concentration remains high, with Cables and Wires accounting for 87% of the revenue mix.
